packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 17 - BLIND IMAGE READING (unverified)

Exposure: Nothing in my context proposed an identification or reading of this text. This is a blind reading.
Beyond the rules: I made enlarged, autocontrast/equalized, rotated (180), mirrored and vertically flipped copies of crops in zoom17/ (a0, a1, ae from image-001; b0, b0e, b1, b1r, b1m, b1f from image-003). I listed only the image-*.jpg filenames in the packet directory to find the images. Nothing else.

IMAGES
- image-001.jpg: overview, two narrow parchment strips (one side) above a cm ruler.
- image-002.jpg: closer view of the same two strips as image-001 (same side; overlapping, not new text).
- image-003.jpg: overview, two strips (presumably the other side, or another pair) above the ruler.
- image-004.jpg: closer view of the same strips as image-003 (overlap).
All four images loaded.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Two horizontal strips per photo, each about 6.5 cm long text area by ~1.3-1.5 cm high, cut from a larger leaf (binding waste type). Each strip carries 2 full lines plus parts of a third cut through ascenders/descenders. The two strips sit edge to edge in the photo; whether they were contiguous on the leaf is not certain (the cut line between them takes out one line that is only partly visible on both edges).
- Script: gothic textualis, black/brown ink, ruled lines visible. Vernacular, looks Dutch/Low German in spelling (observation of letter forms only, e.g. "gh-", "ende"). No rubrics, initials, running titles, glosses or marginalia visible in the cropped area. One possible faint red trace near the middle of the lower strip in image-004 (uncertain).
- Left blank area on each strip in image-001/002 (about 1.2 cm) looks like margin or a pasted-over/abraded zone; in image-003/004 the blank area is on the right. Single column; column width unknown because of crop.
- A white paper/repair or crease runs vertically across the lower strip in image-001/002 at about 60% across.
- Text is not wide enough to judge prose vs verse; lines run on (prose-like), with one punctus mid-line.

SELECTED SPANS: all legible lines on both strips of image-001/002, and the upper strip of image-003/004. The lower strip of image-003/004 remains essentially unread (see below).

TRANSCRIPTION
Side A (image-001, upper strip; also seen in image-002 upper strip)
 image-001 L1: god na mi[.]n[.]n (?minen) deynen (?cleynen) vermoch[ ] (cut at edge; final letter possibly "t"/"h")
 image-001 L2: [n?]atu[.] (first word damaged, ?natu / ?mitt) my hoe?ste (or heeste?) ghemaket na d[ ] (cut)
 image-001 L3: only tops of letters visible; [illegible] ... gh? ... [illegible]

Side A (image-001, lower strip)
 image-001 L4: only lower halves visible: [.]en deel? ... [illegible] ... (cut)
 image-001 L5: gheuen (or ghegeuen?) zitten (?) ende v[.] | [repair/crease] | [.]al?vom? / [.]ap?von? (cut at right edge)
 image-001 L6: onuerdelic? (or onuerdeelt?) [.]?aum? (?rauwe / ?gauw-) . | [crease] | [.]an? / ?dan in ho[ ] (cut)
 Note: there is a punctus after the word before the crease in L6.

Side B (image-003, upper strip; same as image-004 upper strip)
 image-003 L1: [abraded, ?]ouers?/?douers ... gheuen? (or ghelien?) lude? (?liede / ?lieue) meer bych? (?bijch / ?byeh) (cut)
 image-003 L2: [abraded] ... n?h? ... ma(n)nighe? (or manighe) rechte? (?reche) heb[ ] (cut)
 image-003 L3: tops only; [illegible]; a large letter like capital "S" or "L" about two-thirds across.

Side B (image-003, lower strip; image-004 lower strip)
 Letters are visible but do not resolve into words in normal orientation, rotated 180, mirrored, or flipped. Apparent letter shapes in natural orientation: L5 "ouijuouan nochfede?ste?ste ... ", L6 "oe uiq h? ... nuin? rao ? ... dupe?". I suspect this may be offset/show-through or heavily abraded, but I cannot confirm; treat as unread. A tentative interpretation only: the strip may be mounted upside down or reversed relative to its upper partner.

LIMITATIONS
- Strips are narrow; every line is cut at both ends (left by margin/abrasion, right by trimming). Third lines on each strip are cut through.
- Ink is faded and surface rubbed; readings marked ? are uncertain, and word divisions may be wrong.
- Relative order of the two strips and of the two sides is not established from the images.
- Abbreviation marks: none clearly seen; "v[.]" in image-001 L5 may carry a suspension (?ver-).
- Suggest: higher-resolution or raking/UV imaging, especially of the lower strip of image-003/004, and of the abraded left portion of the upper strip of image-003.
